npcs.name: Mira Thistlewood
npcs.hidden_knowledge: Skar did not always lead a bandit clan. Years ago he found a cracked, pulsing red stone -- the Bloodstone Shard -- buried beneath the Old Barrow. It whispers to beasts and twists them fierce and loyal to whoever holds it. The Red Fang Clan is less a bandit gang and more a cult of hunters bound to that stone's will.
follow_up_lines: "I've told you what I know of the stone, dear. Beneath the Old Barrow it stayed hidden for a reason -- best it stays a memory now."
"The Bloodstone's whisper is a hungry thing. Be glad you only heard of it and never had to carry it."
"Some knowledge is a weight, not a gift. You already carry the weight of what I told you about Skar and that stone."
epilogue_follow_up_lines: "With Skar gone, I sleep easier. But I still check the tree line some nights, out of habit more than fear."
"The wolves have gone back to being just wolves, near as I can tell. No more red glint in their eyes. That's your doing."
npcs.epilogue_greeting: Mira sets down her mortar and pestle and smiles properly, for once. "There you are. Come in -- the tea's actually good today."

greeting: Come in, come in, mind the drying herbs overhead.
weather: The mist rolls in thick this time of year, dear. Good for the swamp-root, bad for these old bones.
Rain's coming by nightfall, I'd wager -- the moss on the north wall always curls up first.
crafting: Copper's easy enough to work if you've got oak charcoal hot enough. Bring me hide and I'll show you a poultice recipe.
Old Ferris does the real forging in this village. I just know which leaves stop a wound from souring.
life: Oh, I've tended this garden since before Glenbrook had a proper gate. Seen a lot come and go.
My mother taught me these herbs, and hers before that. Some things in Glenbrook Hollow don't change, thankfully.
quest_hint: Speak plainly with Garrick before you come asking me things, dear. He knows the wolves better than my herbs do.
If the Glades feel wrong to you, trust that feeling. Something's stirring beneath the Old Barrow -- I'd start there.
village: Glenbrook Hollow's smaller than it used to be. Half the old houses past the well stand empty now.
This village survives on stubbornness more than luck, if you ask me. Always has.
opinion_of_player: You've got more patience than most who wander through here. That counts for something in my book.
I trust you more than I did when you first knocked on that door, if that's what you're asking.
rumor: Heard a trader say the roads past the ridge have gone quiet lately. Can't say if that's good news or not.
There's talk of red-tinted rabbits near the Glades again. Old omen, that. Keep your eyes open out there.

life: Funny, I've got more patients coming for scrapes and bruises than poison bites these days. Good problem to have.
aftermath: The Glades feel lighter now, don't they? Even the birds sound less nervous.
Whatever that stone was doing to the wolves, it's done. Properly done, thanks to you.

npcs.blurb: Mira keeps the herb garden behind the well and knows every poultice in the Glades.
greeting_first: Come in, come in, mind the drying herbs overhead. I am Mira, the village herbalist.

opinions.garrick_hale: Garrick? A good man with a bad temper and a worse conscience. He blames himself for his lost patrol. Be patient with him.
opinions.old_ferris: Ferris mends everything in this village, including, I suspect, a few hearts. Do not tell him I said so.
opinions.pip_wren: Pip is a menace and a delight in equal parts. The child has promised everyone a pie and baked none of them yet.
opinions.elowen_moonsong: Elowen keeps the old well in Thornwood. We trade moss and lantern oil, and we share the same stubborn faith in slow things.

healing: Willow bark for fever, yarrow for cuts, healing herb for nearly everything else. Keep a few leaves in your satchel and you will outlast most heroes.
A wound kept clean heals twice as fast. Wash it, bind it, and do not poke it. That is the whole secret, and no one believes me.
food: Berries and herbs fill a pan better than you would think. Cook meat at a fire, never eat it raw, and your stomach will thank you.
Hunger is the quiet killer out there. Eat before you are hungry, not after.
magic: The Glades hum a little under the old stones. I call it the land remembering. Others call it magic and run for the hills.
I am no mage, dear, only a gardener who listens. Plants do not lie about what is wrong with the soil.
animals: Beasts only turn feral for a reason. Hunger, fear, or something whispering in their heads. Find the reason and the wolf is a wolf again.
Rabbits are the first to know. A red-tinted one near the Glades is a very old omen.
shard: The Bloodstone is a hungry thing. I have read enough old herb-lore to fear it, and not enough to explain it.
Whatever sleeps in that red stone, it does not belong to this world's gardens.
family: My mother taught me these herbs and her mother taught her. I never married. The garden was jealous.

stories: My grandmother told of the first Glenbrook, when the barrow was a hill and the hill was a king. They say he asked to be buried with his hounds. They say the hounds still keep watch.
advice: Pick herbs in the morning, when the dew is still on them. They heal better. I do not know why. Ask the herbs.
Do not fight on an empty stomach and do not fight at the very edge of exhaustion. Retreat, bandage, return.

remind: Lark sent you? That bard has a way of stirring up what is better left to settle. Ask me anything, and I will tell it straight.

npcs.requires_hint: There is more to that, dear, but not yet. Ask Garrick Hale about the wolves first, and then come back to me.

npcs.name: Garrick Hale
npcs.hidden_knowledge: The Red Fang Clan's camp sits past the Old Barrow ridge, hidden behind a deadfall you'd walk right past. Garrick lost half his old patrol to a Red Fang raid there and has marked the entrance in his head ever since, but he's never had the nerve -- or the numbers -- to go back.
follow_up_lines: "You know where the camp is. Don't make me say it twice -- just go careful."
"Past the ridge, behind the deadfall. I've told you already. My part's done; the rest is yours."
"I marked that entrance in my head for years and never had the nerve to go back. You do. Don't waste it."
epilogue_follow_up_lines: "That camp's just scorched ground now. Feels strange walking past it and not flinching."
"I went back up to the ridge, after. First time in years. Didn't stay long, but I went."
npcs.epilogue_greeting: Garrick actually looks up when you approach, something almost like relief on his face. "Still in one piece, I see. Good."

weather: Storm's coming. Wolves always get bold before a storm.
Cold snap tonight. Keep a fire going if you're sleeping outside the walls.
crafting: You want a decent blade, take your copper to Old Ferris at the forge. Don't waste good ore on a dull axe.
Ferris can work more than blades, if you ask nice. Armor, arrowheads, whatever you're carrying gear for.
life: Used to run patrols out past the tree line. Different times. Fewer teeth in the dark back then.
Lost good people out there. Don't ask me to talk about it twice.
quest_hint: You want to help? Bring me proof the wolves are turning feral for a reason, not just hunger.
Talk to Mira once you've got something solid. She knows the old stories better than she lets on.
village: Glenbrook's held on through worse than this. Doesn't mean I like watching it get tested again.
This village raised me. I'll not see it torn up by something wearing a wolf's face.
opinion_of_player: You've done more for this place in a few weeks than some folk manage in years. Noted.
Didn't think much of you at first, I'll admit. I was wrong. That's rare for me.
rumor: Heard the Old Barrow's been quieter at night. Might mean nothing. Might mean everything.
Some fool trader's spreading tales about a 'cursed stone' out past the ridge. Wish they'd shut up about it near the children.

life: Might take up patrols again. Not the same as before, but Glenbrook could use eyes on that tree line.
aftermath: Camp's cleared, Skar's dead, and the Glades are quiet. Didn't think I'd live to say that.
Half my old patrol didn't get to see this. I'll carry that. But it's done, and that matters.

npcs.blurb: Garrick walks the gate and the tree line, a retired militia woodsman who does not talk about the old patrol.
greeting_first: Hmph. What do you want?
State your business, stranger. Make it short.

opinions.mira_thistlewood: Mira knows more than she says, and says more than is good for her. But she is honest, and that is rare.
opinions.old_ferris: Ferris. Best smith in a hundred miles and the worst conversationalist. We get on fine.
opinions.reeve_corwin_ashby: Corwin at Kingsford keeps the king's road. Good man. Over-fond of paperwork.
opinions.sylas_underbough: Sylas the ranger? We walked patrols together once. Quiet one. He sees more in a shadow than most see in a candle.

danger: Wolves, boars, and things that should not be wolves. Keep your back to a wall and your blade within reach.
Out past the tree line, everything is hungry. Most things are also stupid. That is your edge.
war: There was a militia once. Forty good people. Do not ask me about it twice.
Wars are loud. The ones that kill you are quiet, and happen in forests.
history: Glenbrook is older than the king's road. Some say older than the king. The barrow predates us all.
classes: Swordsmen hold the line, bowmen thin the pack, rogues cut the throat, mages and alchemists do the strange work. All of them bleed the same.
night: Never be caught beyond the gate after dark if you can help it. Wolves hunt in the dark and they do it well.

about_self: Twenty winters on the militia roster, six on the road before that. I know every tree between here and the Barrow.
stories: The old patrol used to tell a tale of a hound that guarded the Barrow. Big as a calf, eyes like coals. I never saw it. I never went looking either.
advice: Bring more arrows than you think you need. Bring less pride than you think you have.

npcs.name: Old Ferris

greeting: Ferris grunts without looking up from the anvil. "Something broken, or are you just here to talk?"
weather: Rain plays hell with my bellows. Good day to stay in the forge and work.
Cold's good for tempering steel, if nothing else.
crafting: Bring me good copper and hide, I'll turn it into something that doesn't fall apart on you.
Everyone wants Iron before they've earned Leather. Doesn't work like that, whatever your class.
life: Been at this anvil since before Garrick had grey in his beard. Not planning to stop.
Apprenticed under a smith who apprenticed under a smith. That's Glenbrook craft for you.
quest_hint: You want better gear, bring me materials and patience. Neither of us likes shortcuts.
Talk to Mira or Garrick if you want quest business. I just make the pointy bits and the armor bits.
village: Forge's the oldest standing building in Glenbrook besides the well house. Built to last, like everything worth building.
Half this village has walked through my door needing something mended. I don't mind. Keeps me useful.
rumor: Heard the roads have been calmer. Good for trade, good for my ore supply.
Somebody's been asking about a 'shard' with strange heat to it. Can't imagine what that's about.

npcs.epilogue_greeting: Ferris wipes soot from his hands and actually stops working for a moment. "Well. Heard what you did up at that camp. Come in, don't just stand there."

crafting: Whatever's in that shard fragment you're carrying runs hot in a way I've never felt from copper or iron. Bring it here and let me study it properly.

npcs.blurb: Ferris is Glenbrook's blacksmith and has been hammering since before the village got its gate.
greeting_first: Something broken, or just here to talk?
Mind the sparks. What do you need?

opinions.garrick_hale: Garrick has his ghosts. I have my anvil. We keep each other company by saying nothing.
opinions.mira_thistlewood: Mira patches what I break. Only fair I mend her pots in return.
opinions.dorn_ashvale: Dorn runs the quarry forge in Ironhold. Better ore than mine. Worse manners than mine, if you can believe it.
opinions.lark_the_bard: That songbird writes ballads about my forge. Gets the hammer wrong every time.

crafting: Iron wants heat, patience, and the right amount of hate. Copper forgives mistakes. Steel remembers them.
A good edge is not sharp. It is true. Sharp is easy. True takes a lifetime.
money: I charge fair. If a thing is worth fixing, I fix it. If not, I tell you to buy new.
Coin is just metal that other people agreed to believe in. I prefer metal that does something.
history: The forge was here before the gate. I think it was here before the village, to be honest. Funny thing, that.
shard: The shard fragment ran warm in my hand. Warm like blood, not like fire. I put it down more carefully than I would have liked to admit.
war: Soldiers came through, years back. They broke everything. I mended everything. I never did get paid properly.

about_self: Anvil since I was twelve. My father taught me and his father taught him. We have never been rich. We have never been idle either.
stories: I once forged a blade for a captain who said he would pay in gold. He paid in stories. Good ones. I kept the blade-maker's mark on the tang and I think of him whenever I strike.
advice: Keep your gear mended. A cracked buckle kills as dead as a dagger.
npcs.hidden_knowledge: The dwarves who raised the Ironhold forges left a great vault beneath the Dwarven Ruin. Their old runes warm to a blacksmith's touch. I have been meaning to go for thirty years. I am too old now. You are not.
follow_up_lines: The Dwarven Ruin lies south of the quarry. I told you what I know. Take a hammer, not a sword.
Dwarven runes warm to a smith. If it hums, do not be alarmed. It is happy to see you.

remind: Lark sent you? Fine. The shard fragment ran warm in my hands. Tell the bard I said it was a plain stone to start with, and an ill one now.

npcs.name: Pip Wren
npcs.blurb: Pip is Glenbrook's youngest berry-picker and loudest promise-maker.
greeting_first: Hello! Hello! Are you a hero? You look like a hero. Do you like pie?

opinions.mira_thistlewood: Mira is the best. She gave me a whole honey cake once. Also she promised me a pie. Do you know where it is?
opinions.garrick_hale: Garrick is scary but he let me hold his axe once. Do not tell anyone.
opinions.old_ferris: Ferris lets me work the bellows! It is so hot!

food: Berries are the best. Purple ones for pie, red ones for jam, and green ones are for bad ideas.
I ate nine berries once and my tongue turned purple for a week. Worth it.
animals: Rabbits! Have you seen the red ones? They look at you funny. Garrick says do not touch.
I want a pet boar. Mira says no. Garrick says definitely no.
family: I live with Aunt Wren by the well. She says I talk too much. I do not think that is possible.
danger: Wolves are scary but boars are scarier because they are grumpy. Stay away from grumpy things!
night: I am not allowed outside after dark. Something makes noises in the Glades. Aunt Wren says it is owls. I say it is bigger than owls.

about_self: I am Pip! I pick berries, I carry baskets, and I am going to be a famous baker. Soon. Right after the berries.
home_lines: Glenbrook is the best village ever. We have a well, a smithy, a herbalist, and me!
rumors: I heard there is a haunted hill with a hound that never sleeps. I did not hear it from anyone important though.
Somebody said the red wolves are getting braver. I just stay out of the tall grass.
stories: Once upon a time a berry was so sweet that every wolf in the Glades came to ask for one. The berry said no, and the wolves went home sad. The end. I made that up.
opinion_player: You are my favourite hero so far! You are the only hero so far, but still!

give: Mira promised me a pie if I bring her five Glade Berries, but I keep eating them on the way. Could you pick five for me? The bushes around the village are full of them!
remind: Five Glade Berries! Mira is going to make a pie and I will give you the first slice. Probably.
done: Oh! They are perfect! Purple and everything! Here, take this. I got it from Mira, but it is yours now.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: Do not tell anyone, but I found a tiny cave behind the waterfall at Glade Pond. There is a glowing stone in it. I did not touch it. It looked grumpy.
follow_up_lines: I showed you the cave. Do not tell Garrick, okay? He will say it is dangerous.

npcs.name: Reeve Corwin Ashby
npcs.blurb: Corwin keeps the king's road and Kingsford's ledgers, in that order.
greeting_first: Welcome to Kingsford. I am Reeve Ashby. Mind the road, mind the law, and do not feed the geese.

opinions.bess_hartwell: Bess Hartwell runs the best inn on the road and the worst tab policy in the county.
opinions.lark_the_bard: Lark? Charming. Brings in half the trade. Owes me for a lute I never saw.
opinions.old_maud_fennick: Old Maud's farm feeds half Kingsford. She is rude to me, which I take as respect.
opinions.garrick_hale: Garrick Hale of Glenbrook. We served together. He does not write, but he is the best tracker I know.

money: Tolls fund the road, the road feeds the town, the town pays the tolls. It is a circle, and I am in the middle of it.
I keep careful ledgers. When the coin runs short, I know exactly who to ask.
war: The king's patrols are thin out here. I make do with farmers, bows, and prayers.
Bandits grow bold when the garrison is far. We do what we can.
danger: Wolves on the road, boars in the barley, and bandits in the bluff at Bandit Lookout. Travel in the morning, camp in a village.
travel: The king's road runs east to the hills and west to the Glades. Stay on it and you will rarely meet a bear. Leave it and you will meet everything else.
history: Kingsford is named for the ford, not the king. The king came later and took the credit.

about_self: I have kept this ford for twelve years. The ledgers are tidy, the gate is oiled, and the road is mostly safe. That last part is why I need your help.
home_lines: Kingsford sits where the king's road crosses the river. Everyone passes through. Few stay. I try to make it worth staying.
rumors: Highwaymen have been spotted near Bandit Lookout. The patrols cannot spare the men.
A caravan from the dunes arrives next week. It will bring spice, silks, and trouble.
stories: The ford was a battleground once. They say the river still runs red every anniversary. I have checked. It does not. Mostly.

give: Wolves and boars have been harrying travellers on the Highmeadow roads. I need five of them dealt with. Do that and the road will be safe enough for the next caravan.
remind: Five beasts on the roads around Kingsford, if you please. Fewer wolves means fewer funerals.
done: The road is quieter. The merchants will notice, and so will I. The ledgers will say you earned this.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: Bandit Lookout, south-east of town, is where the highwaymen gather. They have a captain, hired by someone who is not a bandit. I do not know who. If you go, go carefully, and tell no one at the inn.
follow_up_lines: I told you what I know of the bandits. It is not much, but it is more than the town knows.

npcs.name: Bess Hartwell
npcs.blurb: Bess runs the Hartwell Inn, where every traveller on the king's road eventually sits down.
greeting_first: Sit, sit! Mind the floor, I just scrubbed it. What can I get you, love?

opinions.reeve_corwin_ashby: Corwin pays his tab on time and tips in advice. Good man, bad tipper.
opinions.lark_the_bard: Lark sings for his supper and sometimes for mine. I let him, because the customers like it.
opinions.zahra_qasim: Zahra from the Dust Bazaar? Sharpest trader on the road. Sells me spice at a price that hurts and a flavour that heals.

food: Stew, bread, and a pint. That is the whole menu, and it is enough. When we have meat, it is a feast.
Cooked meat is worth its weight in silver out here. Raw is worth a bad stomach.
money: I charge fair. Not cheap, fair. Cheap is how you end up with bad meat and good lawyers.
music: Lark plays on Fridays. If you are here on a Friday, bring ear-plugs or a very forgiving heart.
travel: I hear everything travellers say. The south road is quiet, the east road is bandits, and the west road smells of wet dog.
family: My husband passed three winters back. The inn keeps me busy and the busy keeps me sane.

about_self: I was born at the inn. My mother kept it, her mother before her. I plan to die at the inn. Not soon, mind.
home_lines: Kingsford is where the road gets its supper. Everyone stops here. It is a good place to be if you like hearing gossip.
rumors: I heard from a caravan driver that the dunes are full of scorpions the size of dogs. I hope he was joking.
A traveller said there is an oasis in the desert with a keeper who never sleeps.
stories: A traveller once left a pearl in payment. It was worth more than the inn. I returned it. He never came back. I still keep the room warm.

give: The larder is bare and the stew pot nearly dry. Four portions of cooked meat is all I need. Hunt something, cook it at a campfire, and bring it here, love.
remind: Four portions of cooked meat, love. Hunt, cook, bring. The inn is counting on you.
done: You are a lifesaver! The guests will eat tonight, and so will you. Sit, sit, a free supper for you.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: There is a hidden room under the inn, my husband's wine cellar. I still do not go down. If you want to look, the key is above the lintel. Mind the spiders.
follow_up_lines: The cellar is yours to look at. Take what you like, but leave the portrait on the wall.

npcs.name: Lark
npcs.blurb: Lark sings for coin, supper, and the next good story, and has walked every road worth walking.
greeting_first: Ah, a new face for the chorus! I am Lark, and if you have a story, I will trade a verse for it.

opinions.bess_hartwell: Bess! The heart of the Hartwell and the lungs of Kingsford. She feeds a bard, and a bard is grateful.
opinions.old_ferris: Ferris is a hammer in the shape of a man. His forge is a song of its own, if one listens.
opinions.mira_thistlewood: Mira is all green things and gentle warnings. A fine verse waiting for a fine rhyme.
opinions.reeve_corwin_ashby: Corwin has a heart under all those ledgers. I put it in a verse once. He asked me to remove it.

music: A lute in the right hands is worth ten swords. Songs outlast kings. Remember that when you choose your battles.
Every village has a song. If you listen, they tell you where the ghosts are.
history: The old kings left no bones, only ballads. Every ballad is half a lie and half a prayer.
I collect stories the way Ferris collects ore. Slowly, and with an eye for the good bits.
travel: I walk the roads because the roads walk me. Highmeadow, Thornwood, the dunes, the coast. Each one a different key.
shard: The Bloodstone Shard! A tale of red fire and whispering beasts. Ferris and Mira each know a verse. I am gathering them for a ballad.
gods: The old gods are in the stones, the moon, and the sea. I sing to all of them. One of them is bound to listen.

about_self: I was born in a cart on the road to Kingsford. I have been singing since before I could speak. People say that explains a lot.
home_lines: Kingsford is where the roads meet and where the audiences are. The Hartwell Inn is my stage, my bed, and my creditor.
rumors: They say the Hollow Peaks have a hermit who talks to the snow. I want to hear what it says.
There is a lighthouse on the coast whose keeper sings to the waves. I would give a year of coin for that song.
stories: There was a king who could not sleep because the moon laughed at him. He climbed the highest peak to scold it. The moon dropped a snowflake on his nose. He has slept ever since.
jokes: Why did the bard cross the road? To get to the other verse.

give: I am writing a ballad of the Bloodstone and want the real tale from people who live it. Old Ferris in Glenbrook and Mira Thistlewood each know a verse. Ask them, then sing the answer back to me.
remind: Ferris and Mira, my friend. Their stories are the heart of my ballad. Bring them back when you have them.
done: Magnificent! Ferris and Mira both gave you gold, and now I shall spin it into silver. The ballad is nearly finished. Here, take a verse of thanks and a few coins besides.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: Between songs I have learned that the highwaymen at Bandit Lookout are paid by someone in Kingsford. A tune I overheard. I do not know who. The Reeve would want to know, but trust no one with the name yet.
follow_up_lines: I sang you my secret and it is out in the world now. Do be careful with it.

npcs.name: Old Maud Fennick
npcs.blurb: Maud works the barley fields at Harvest Farm and feeds half of Kingsford.
greeting_first: You are standing in my barley. Step out of it. Now, what do you want?

opinions.reeve_corwin_ashby: Corwin the reeve counts my barley sacks and charges me the toll. He is a good boy, but he fusses.
opinions.bess_hartwell: Bess buys my barley. She pays on time and pours generous. I like her.

weather: Rain in the barley is worth gold. Rain in the hay is worth grief. I read the sky every morning.
The wind tells me when the harvest is coming. It is coming now.
food: Barley bread, barley stew, barley beer. If you do not like barley, you will go hungry in Highmeadow.
Fresh bread is the one luxury I allow myself. Do not ask for butter.
animals: Boars rooting up the rows, deer nibbling the sprouts, crows eating the rest. I fight them all and win about half.
family: My boys left for the coast and never wrote. The fields write to me every morning. I answer with a hoe.
danger: The road is safe in the day. At night the boars come out. Do not walk the rows after dark.

about_self: Fifty harvests on this land. My husband went in the sixth. I plan to follow him in the sixtieth.
home_lines: Harvest Farm has fed Kingsford since before the road was paved. The soil is good, the neighbours are bad, and the barley is perfect.
rumors: Something large has been leaving tracks in the north field. Not a boar. Bigger.
The windmill to the east has not turned in a year. Somebody has been sleeping in it.
stories: My grandmother swore the old windmill grinds flour on nights with no wind. I have never seen it. I have never gone to look either.

give: Something is rooting up my barley at night. Boars, I suspect. Drive off four of them and I will be in your debt, and I do not like being in debt.
remind: Four boars, near the farm. Do not argue with them. Just kill them.
done: Good riddance. The barley will live another season. Here, take a loaf. Do not tell anyone I was nice.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The old windmill to the east has a cellar. Last winter I found a bag of coin in it, left by someone in a hurry. I took only enough to replace my plough. The rest is still there, if you are fond of risk.
follow_up_lines: The windmill is east. Do not bring me any trouble. I have enough of my own.

npcs.name: Sylas Underbough
npcs.blurb: Sylas watches the Thornwood trails and says little about what he sees.
greeting_first: You walk loud. Sit by the fire; the trees are listening enough as it is.

opinions.elowen_moonsong: Elowen tends the Moonwell. I guard the path to it. We rarely speak, which is how we like it.
opinions.garrick_hale: Garrick and I walked patrols together. He talks less than I do. That takes skill.
opinions.captain_ysolde_varn: Ysolde holds the pass above us. If she calls for aid, I go. That is all that needs saying.

danger: Shadow wolves hunt at dusk. Bone soldiers walk the old road at night. Neither one tires.
The Thornwood bites back. Keep to the trails and out of the briars.
animals: The wolves here are bigger than in the Glades, and darker. Something about the shade, I think.
night: Never camp under a thorn tree. They lean in toward the warmth.
history: Old soldiers fell here. Some still walk. I do not disturb them and they do not disturb me, mostly.

about_self: Ranger for nineteen years. I know every path, every bog, and every bad idea in Thornwood.
home_lines: The Lodge is the last safe fire before the deep wood. Stay warm, then go carefully.
rumors: Spiders have taken the old den to the north. I do not go there anymore.
The Moonwell water has been glowing brighter these past nights. Elowen will not say why.
stories: A ranger once followed a white stag into the thorns and never came out. They say the stag still waits for a second follower.

give: Patrol with me, in spirit anyway. Check the Moonwell, thin the shadow wolves along the trail, and report back. Five should do.
remind: Moonwell, then five wolves of the shadow kind, then me. In that order if you like.
done: The trail is quieter. Good work. Take this, and keep your eyes up.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: There is a hollow in the old ruins where the bone soldiers rise. Something calls them there. Bring a torch, and do not go alone.
follow_up_lines: The ruins are where I said. Do not wake what you cannot put back down.

npcs.name: Elowen Moonsong
npcs.blurb: Elowen keeps the Moonwell and listens to what the water remembers.
greeting_first: The water told me you were coming. It was less specific about why.

opinions.sylas_underbough: Sylas keeps the path clear. Humans call that duty. The wood calls it friendship.
opinions.mira_thistlewood: Mira and I trade herbs and silence. Both are rare.
opinions.brannoch_the_hermit: Brannoch speaks to snow. I speak to water. We understand each other better than we admit.

magic: Magic is attention, nothing more. The well has been paid attention to for a thousand years. It remembers.
Moonlight, still water, and an open mind. That is most of the craft.
gods: The old powers sleep in the wells and the stones. Do not wake them. Do not insult them either.
night: Night is when the water is clearest. Come at midnight and you will see more than your own face.
shard: The red stone cries to the water. The water does not answer. That silence troubles me.
healing: Moonwell water heals what has been wounded by darkness. It does little for broken bones, sadly.

about_self: I have kept this well since before your grandmother. I will keep it after you are gone. That is not a threat; it is a comfort.
home_lines: The Moonwell glows when the night is thin. Tonight is thin. Sit if you wish.
rumors: The wolves are crueler this year. The water says something has stirred them from below.
stories: A traveller once asked the well for a wish. It gave him a reflection that looked back. He has not asked since.

give: The rite needs pine resin, three lumps, taken from the old pines of the Thornwood. Bring them and I will light the water.
remind: Three lumps of pine resin. The pines are patient. So must you be.
done: The Moonwell shines. Take a measure of its light with you. It will not last, but neither will the dark.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: Beneath the Hollow Peaks there is a cave where a hermit hears the snow speak. He once told me the mountains are older than the sky. Go to him, gently.
follow_up_lines: The hermit will receive you if you are quiet. Bring him a bloom from the frost.

npcs.name: Captain Ysolde Varn
npcs.blurb: Ysolde commands Frostwatch Outpost and holds the pass against whatever comes down the mountain.
greeting_first: State your name and purpose. Quickly. The cold does not wait.

opinions.brannoch_the_hermit: The hermit is harmless and half-mad. He also predicted the last avalanche, so I do not laugh.
opinions.sylas_underbough: Sylas sends word when the Thornwood stirs. I send him soup when it does not. Fair trade.

war: We hold the pass. That is all. If it falls, the lowlands burn.
Seventeen soldiers, one wall, one pass. Not poor odds if you are stubborn enough.
danger: Snow wolves in packs, frost bears at the ridge, ice wisps near the lake. Dress warm and move fast.
weather: The wind here has teeth. If it tells you to turn back, listen.
history: The outpost was built by a king who never saw it. We keep his orders anyway.

about_self: Twenty-two years of service, eleven in the Peaks. I have lost a toe, two friends, and my patience for fools.
home_lines: Frostwatch is cold, cramped, and ours. Warm yourself and move along.
rumors: Wolves have been coming down the pass in larger numbers than usual. The snow is not feeding them well.
stories: A sentry once saw a white bear stand on its hind legs and bow to the moon. He was relieved of duty. I believe him.

give: Snow wolves are gathering on the pass. Kill six of them and report to me. We hold this line together.
remind: Six snow wolves on the pass. The wall is counting on you.
done: The pass is clearer. You have earned a place at our fire. And this.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: There is a frozen lake east of the outpost. Beneath the ice, something pulses. The sentries say it is a trick of the light. I say we should not test that.
follow_up_lines: The lake is east. Do not walk on it. I will not explain twice.

npcs.name: Brannoch the Hermit
npcs.blurb: Brannoch lives alone in a cave on the mountainside and says the snow tells him things.
greeting_first: Hello, hello. The snow said you were coming. It did not say you were kind. Are you?

opinions.captain_ysolde_varn: The Captain frowns at me, and then brings me firewood. A fair woman.
opinions.elowen_moonsong: Elowen listens to water. I listen to snow. We should compare notes more.

weather: The snow falls in a rhythm if you listen. Three soft, one hard. That means a storm.
The wind is a child that never grew up. Humour it.
magic: Magic is just the mountain remembering itself. I only help it along.
gods: There are gods in the high places. They are shy. Do not stare.
animals: The frost bears are lonely. So are the wolves. Everyone up here is lonely.
history: Before the kingdoms the mountains were already old. They will outlast the next kingdom too.

about_self: I came up here to think for a week. That was forty years ago. The week is not quite done.
home_lines: This cave is warm because I sing to it. The cave likes songs, mostly sad ones.
rumors: The summit shrine hums at night. I have not climbed to see why. I am old, not foolish.
stories: Once the moon fell asleep over the peaks and the snow tucked her in. In the morning there was a lake. That is the whole story.

give: Frost blooms grow in the cold hollows. Two of them, please. They keep the snow from forgetting my name.
remind: Two frost blooms. The hollows hide them well. Look where the snow is thinnest.
done: Beautiful! The snow shall remember me another winter. Take this, and a blessing.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: At the summit there is a shrine older than the mountains' names. The snow gathers there like a congregation. Bring respect, not a sword.
follow_up_lines: The shrine is waiting. Go gently, and say hello for me.

npcs.name: Dorn Ashvale
npcs.blurb: Dorn runs the Ironhold quarry and its forge, and prides himself on never losing a worker.
greeting_first: Mind the loose rock. Mind your feet. Mind your tongue. In that order.

opinions.hilde_coppergate: Hilde runs the Deepvein mine. Tough as flint. We argue about prices and respect each other for it.
opinions.old_ferris: Ferris from Glenbrook? Good hands, small forge. I send him my seconds and he makes them sing.

crafting: Iron ore, coal, a hot forge, and patience. Everything else is decoration.
A good blade comes from good ore. I only mine good ore.
money: I pay my men fair and on time. That is all the secret there is.
danger: Hill brigands raid the carts. Rock golems wander in from the tarn. Take a friend or take a shield.
history: Dwarves worked these hills before us. Their tunnels run deeper than the maps say.

about_self: Thirty years at the quarry. I have broken eleven hammers and four bones, and I regret none of them.
home_lines: The quarry feeds a dozen forges. Everything strong in the east began as this rock.
rumors: Golems have been waking near the tarn. They never did that before.
The brigands at the slag camp are well-armed. Someone is feeding them steel.
stories: My grandfather swore he heard the mountain breathe one night. We put new beams in the next day. The old ones cracked.

give: The forge is hungry. Bring me five iron ore from the veins around the quarry. I will pay you in coin and in steel.
remind: Five iron ore. Swing a pick, or take it off a golem. I am not choosy.
done: Good ore. Good work. Here is your pay, and a bit extra for not complaining.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: There is a slag camp south of the quarry where the brigands smelt stolen steel. Their leader is not a fool. If you go, strike fast and leave no one to warn the rest.
follow_up_lines: You know where the slag camp is. Do not make me regret telling you.

npcs.name: Hilde Coppergate
npcs.blurb: Hilde has run the Deepvein Mine for fifteen years and has not lost a miner to the dark yet.
greeting_first: Hard hat or no hat, I do not care, but do not stand under the supports. What do you need?

opinions.dorn_ashvale: Dorn Ashvale and his quarry. We swap ore and insults. I have yet to lose either contest.

danger: The deep levels have things in them that do not like lamps. I lost a lantern last week. I do not know what took it.
Rock golems rise when the ground shakes. I have stopped counting.
money: Copper and iron pay the bills. Silver pays the debts. Gold I have only heard of.
history: The first shaft was dug by dwarves. We only widened it.
family: My crew is my family. I have no other, and I would like to keep it that way.

about_self: I have been underground for thirty years. I have never seen the sky look as good as when I leave.
home_lines: Deepvein runs deep. Do not go below the third level without a rope and a friend.
rumors: There are noises in the lower tunnels. My miners say it is the rock settling. I say rock does not whisper.
stories: An old miner swore he saw a golem kneel and weep. He quit that week and became a baker.

give: Something is creeping through the upper tunnels. Five of them. Clear them out and report back.
remind: Five creatures in the upper tunnels. My crew will not go back until they are gone.
done: The tunnels are clear. My crew breathes again. You have earned a share of the vein.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The old dwarven ruin is connected to the lower mine. I sealed the passage years ago. If you want to open it, the key is a hammer-strike on the third beam, twice. Do not tell Dorn.
follow_up_lines: The passage is sealed for a reason. Open it only if you are sure.

npcs.name: Zahra Qasim
npcs.blurb: Zahra trades spices, silks, and rumours at the Dust Bazaar, and has never lost a bargain.
greeting_first: Welcome, welcome, friend! Spice for your stew, silk for your sweetheart, or news for a coin?

opinions.bess_hartwell: Bess of Kingsford drives a hard bargain with a soft smile. I admire her enormously and avoid her at the market.
opinions.tamsin_the_well_keeper: Tamsin keeps the oasis well. Without her, my caravans would die of thirst. I send her gifts and pretend they are for business.

money: Everything has a price, my friend. Even this advice. First one is free, the second costs you a smile.
Gold is a language. Learn it and the whole world will speak to you.
food: Saffron, cumin, dried peppers, and dates. Add to any stew and you will think you are rich.
travel: The dunes shift. The oases do not, but the roads between them do. Keep a guide or keep a compass.
danger: Jackals hunt in packs, scorpions hide in the sand, and dust wraiths come with the wind. I pay guards well for a reason.
weather: The sun is a merchant too. It takes everything and gives shade for a price.

about_self: I started with one camel and a sack of cumin. Now I have a stall, three camels, and a tendency to give speeches.
home_lines: The Dust Bazaar never closes. Come at dawn for the best prices and at dusk for the best stories.
rumors: There is a temple half-buried in the dunes. They say it hums at noon.
Scorpions the size of dogs have been seen near the pit. I pay triple for chitin.
stories: A merchant once sold a mirage to a king. The king paid in full and never complained. I think about that often.
trade_lines: I trade in spices and gossip. Your coin buys the first and your attention the second.

give: Scorpion chitin! Three pieces, if you please. It makes the best lacquer and I pay triple. Bring them to me and we both profit.
remind: Three pieces of scorpion chitin. The pit is south of here. Mind the stingers.
done: Excellent! Fine quality. Here is your pay, and a little extra. Do not tell my competitors.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The Sun Temple is not empty. Something keeps the sand from covering its door. I have a map, and I am willing to share it for a smile and your trust.
follow_up_lines: The temple is where the map says. If you find gold, remember who gave you the map.

npcs.name: Tamsin the Well-Keeper
npcs.blurb: Tamsin tends the oasis well and gives water to every traveller who asks.
greeting_first: Drink first, then talk. The desert has no patience for the thirsty.

opinions.zahra_qasim: Zahra is a hard bargainer but a good soul. She has never let my well run dry.

weather: The sun comes up like a hammer and goes down like a prayer. In between, drink water.
danger: Jackals at dusk, scorpions at noon, and wraiths when the wind rises. Stay near the well and you will be fine.
travel: The dunes shift every night. Trust your feet less than the stars.
healing: Water, shade, and rest. If they do not work, more of the same.
family: My mother kept this well, and hers before her. I have no children. The well will have to do.

about_self: Forty summers at the oasis. I have given water to kings and beggars. They drink the same.
home_lines: The oasis is the only green for a hundred miles. Respect it and it will respect you.
rumors: Wraiths have been circling nearer than usual. I think the old temple is stirring.
stories: A traveller once asked the well to show his future. It showed him a glass of water. He was disappointed. He lived to be ninety.

give: Jackals have been stalking the oasis at dusk. Five of them would settle the matter. Please, I cannot do it myself anymore.
remind: Five jackals near the oasis, dear. I will sleep better when they are gone.
done: Thank you. The oasis breathes easier. Take this, and drink whenever you wish.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: Beneath the oasis there is a spring that never dries. I have never told anyone, and I will tell you if you promise to protect it. The source is the Sun Temple's cistern, I believe.
follow_up_lines: You know the secret now. Guard it well.

npcs.name: Odo Saltmarsh
npcs.blurb: Odo has kept the Gull Point light burning for thirty years and talks to the sea more than to people.
greeting_first: Ahoy, landlubber. Mind the stairs, they are steeper than they look.

opinions.nell_tidewater: Nell down at the harbor? Sharp as a hook and twice as honest. She brings me bread when the fog sets in.

weather: Storm by sundown, I would wager. The gulls have gone quiet.
Fog in the morning, sun at noon, rain at night. The coast never makes up its mind.
history: The light was built after a hundred ships went down in a single winter. We do not forget them.
danger: Shore crabs on the rocks, drowned sailors in the surf, and worse in the cove. Watch your footing.
travel: The coast road is the safest way south. The sea road is the fastest way to the bottom.
gods: The sea has her own gods. They do not like to be named. I leave them an offering and a candle.

about_self: Thirty years of oil, wick, and weather. I have seen a ship lost and a ship saved, and I do not know which I think of more.
home_lines: Gull Point is the end of the world, or the start. Depends on your direction.
rumors: There is a wreck in the cove with a ghost crew. They signal at midnight. I do not signal back.
Smugglers use the tidecaller cave. The tide hides their boats. I pretend not to see.
stories: The lamp once guided a ship home that had been dead for a century. The crew waved and sailed on into the fog. I wave back every night.

give: The light needs oil, and the oil needs kelp, four fronds of sea kelp from the rocks below. Bring them and the lamp will burn through the storm.
remind: Four fronds of sea kelp, from the shore rocks. The storm will not wait.
done: The lamp burns bright. Ships will find home tonight. You have my thanks, landlubber.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The wreck in Wreck Cove is the Marigold, a ship I watched go down. Her captain still keeps a locked chest in the hold. I could never bring myself to look. Maybe you can.
follow_up_lines: The wreck is south of the harbor. If you find the chest, leave me out of it.

npcs.name: Nell Tidewater
npcs.blurb: Nell runs the fish stall at Driftwood Harbor and knows every boat by its creak.
greeting_first: Fresh catch, fresh gossip, fresh bread. Pick one or take all three, love!

opinions.odo_saltmarsh: Old Odo keeps the light. Grumpy as a barnacle and just as stubborn. I love him dearly.
opinions.bess_hartwell: Bess at Kingsford buys my smoked fish. She also complains about the smell. That is how we know we are friends.

food: Smoked herring, salt cod, and eel stew. If it swims, I can cook it.
Never eat a fish that looks back at you. Unless it is very fresh.
weather: Wind from the west, rain by noon. My knees are never wrong.
money: Pearls pay well, but the divers pay with fingers. I pay in fish.
travel: Boats go up and down the coast. I know every captain and half their debts.
family: My husband went to sea and sent a postcard from every port. Then he stopped. I kept the postcards.

about_self: I came to the harbor as a girl and I will leave it as a legend, or a fish. Whichever comes first.
home_lines: Driftwood Harbor is built from what the tide leaves. We are all driftwood here.
rumors: A pearl diver brought up something strange last week. Black, round, humming. He sold it before I could look.
Smugglers are working the north cove again. The tide helps them.
stories: They say a mermaid once bargained for a net. She gave a pearl and took the net home. The fish have been scarce since.

give: The divers will not go down this week, it is rough water. I need two pearl shells, love. Find them along the shore rocks and I will pay well.
remind: Two pearl shells from the shore. The tide leaves them just below the high mark.
done: Lovely! Just lovely. Here is your pay and a bit of smoked fish besides.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The smugglers meet in a camp hidden past the north rocks. The tide cuts the path twice a day. If you go at low tide, you can reach them dry-footed. They pay a lot of people to look away. I did not take their coin.
follow_up_lines: Low tide, north rocks. I told you what I know. The rest is your business.

npcs.name: Marrow Vane
npcs.blurb: Marrow Vane brews swamp potions and mutters to her cauldron, which mutters back.
greeting_first: Hee! A visitor! Mind the toads, they bite. Mind the cauldron, it bites harder.

opinions.brother_alder: Brother Alder prays in a haunted chapel. I brew in a haunted hut. We are both quite mad, but he is politer about it.

magic: Magic is stew with intent. Add what the swamp offers and stir clockwise.
Bog lilies for sorrow, glowcaps for courage. Mix and you have a fine soup.
animals: Toads hear everything. Lurkers hear more. Never trust a quiet swamp.
danger: Lurkers pull travellers under. Bog boars charge when startled. And the fen has other things besides.
healing: Swamp-water poultice for cuts. Peat tea for fever. Never mix the two.
food: I eat what the swamp feeds me. Do not ask what.

about_self: I was a scholar once. Then I learned the swamp knows more than books. Now I am a witch. Much better hours.
home_lines: Mossfen Hut stands where the ground stays dry. The only dry spot for a mile. Be grateful.
rumors: The old chapel is sinking. The bell tolls on its own. Brother Alder pretends not to hear it.
Something at the leech pools is eating the leeches. I would like to know what.
stories: A traveller once asked my cauldron for the future. It showed him a bowl of soup. He ate the soup. He was happy.

give: My brew wants three bog lilies and two glowcaps. Pick them from the fen, but mind where you step. Hee!
remind: Three bog lilies, two glowcaps. The brew is getting impatient.
done: Perfect! The cauldron approves. Take a vial of the finished brew. Do not sip it in front of strangers.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The drowned hollow to the south holds a sunken village. At low water you can see rooftops. The people did not drown, they were drowned, and their bell still rings beneath the water.
follow_up_lines: The hollow is where I told you. Do not drink the water.

npcs.name: Brother Alder
npcs.blurb: Brother Alder keeps a chapel the swamp is slowly swallowing and prays for those who rest beneath it.
greeting_first: Peace upon you, traveller. Mind the water; it rises faster than prayer.

opinions.marrow_vane: Marrow is a witch, or so she claims. I find her kinder than most priests. Do not tell my bishop.

gods: I pray to whatever listens. The chapel has heard many gods and kept none.
Faith is a candle in a damp room. It flickers, but it still counts.
history: The chapel was built on dry ground. The ground changed its mind.
danger: The dead here are restless. They do not mean harm, but they do not know the difference anymore.
night: At night the bell tolls. I used to ring it. Now I only listen.
healing: I tend the sick when they come. Most come too late. I bury them kindly.

about_self: I came here to serve. I stayed to keep company with the forgotten.
home_lines: The chapel is sinking by an inch each year. I have measured. It is oddly comforting.
rumors: Restless dead walk the chapel grounds. I have taken to leaving them candles.
A witch lives in the hut north of here. She makes soup that glows. I do not ask.
stories: The first priest of this chapel swore the swamp would give back what it took. It has not yet. I am patient.

give: The dead are restless. Four of them have wandered into the chapel grounds. Lay them to rest, and I will be in your debt.
remind: Four restless dead, near the chapel. Be gentle, if you can.
done: Peace at last. The chapel is quiet. Take this, with my blessing.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: Beneath the chapel there is a crypt that was sealed long ago. The names on the door are worn smooth, but I remember them. If you must go, say each one aloud first.
follow_up_lines: The crypt is below. Speak the names. They will answer.

npcs.name: Ignatius Vale
npcs.blurb: Ignatius studies the Ashen Wastes' fire and stone, and has not noticed that it is trying to kill him.
greeting_first: Fascinating! A living person! Quickly, do you know the melting point of obsidian?

history: The Ashen Legion marched here in the old wars and burned. Their ghosts still drill in the ash. Fascinating, really.
Ruined cities beneath ruined cities. That is the Ashen Wastes in a sentence.
magic: The fire here is not natural. It thinks. I have notes, if you would like to read them. Seventeen volumes.
danger: Cinder hounds, ember golems, ash wraiths, and ashen knights. I find them all instructive.
crafting: Obsidian cuts finer than steel and shatters like a promise. Sulfur burns brighter than anything honest.
weather: The ash falls like snow. It does not melt. It buries.

about_self: I was a scholar of the Royal Academy. I came here to study the flames and was relieved of my chair for my enthusiasm.
home_lines: The Cinder Ruins were a city once. Now they are a laboratory. My laboratory.
rumors: There is a throne at the heart of the wastes. The fire sits on it. I do not recommend a visit.
The obsidian spire hums when the volcano breathes. I have measured it.
stories: A knight once walked into the fire to prove his courage. The fire politely declined him. He was sent home with a mild scorch.

give: For my research I need three samples of sulfur and two of obsidian. Gather them from the wastes. I would do it myself, but I am rather busy being fascinated.
remind: Three sulfur, two obsidian. The wastes provide, if you survive them.
done: Magnificent samples! Here is your payment, and a note of thanks for my footnotes.

npcs.hidden_knowledge: The Ember Throne sits at the heart of the wastes, and something sits upon it. I have measured its heat from afar. It is not a volcano. It is a king, and it is awake.
follow_up_lines: The throne is east. Do not go unprepared. Do not go, in fact. But you will.
